findings.evidence: roadmap/EpsilonEridaniRoadmaps/SmallXAndSaturation/README.md:328-330: "the derived `size` (the difference) and `impactParameter` (the midpoint) and the simp lemmas reconstructing the endpoints from them". Every other projection lemma in the file (`size_add`, `impactParameter_smul`, `size_ofSizeImpactParameter`, …) is `@[simp]`; these two are the only reconstruction lemmas and are plain `lemma`s.
findings.fix: Add `@[simp]` to both. Both LHSs are headed by `HAdd`/`HSub` of `impactParameter d` and `size d` of the same `d` and rewrite to a strictly simpler RHS, so they terminate and cannot overlap `impactParameter_add` / `size_add`.
findings.issue: `impactParameter_add_size` (line 216) and `impactParameter_sub_size` (line 222) are exactly the endpoint-reconstruction lemmas §0.1 names, but neither carries `@[simp]`, so `b + 2⁻¹ • r` and `b - 2⁻¹ • r` never normalise back to `d.quark` / `d.antiquark` for a consumer.

findings.evidence: upstream/mathlib/Mathlib/Basic/NNReal/Defs.lean:283 `instance {M : Type*} [AddCommMonoid M] [Module ℝ M] : Module ℝ≥0 M`, which gives both `SMul ℝ≥0 (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))` (feeding the generic instance at line 88) and `SMul ℝ≥0 Dipole` (from `Module ℝ Dipole` at line 120). The only use of the generic instance in this file is supplying `SMul ℕ`/`SMul ℤ` to `Function.Injective.addCommGroup` (lines 115-118).
findings.fix: Replace the unbounded instance with the three the transfers actually need — `SMul ℕ Dipole`, `SMul ℤ Dipole`, `SMul ℝ Dipole` — and state `smul_quark`/`smul_antiquark` for those, so no lawless action is exported and no second `SMul ℝ≥0 Dipole` path arises.
findings.issue: `instance {S : Type*} [SMul S (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))] : SMul S Dipole` publishes `•` for every scalar type acting on the plane, but the only laws provided are `Module ℝ Dipole` and the ℝ-only `size_smul` / `impactParameter_smul` (lines 207, 210). For e.g. `S = ℝ≥0` a user gets `c • d` with no `MulAction`/`DistribMulAction`/`Module`, no `one_smul`, and no way to compute its size or impact parameter. It also collides with the `SMul ℝ≥0 Dipole` that Mathlib derives from `Module ℝ Dipole`, so two resolution paths exist for the same notation and the generic `smul_quark`/`smul_antiquark` need not match syntactically.

findings.evidence: Coordinates.lean:91-113 and 216-225 pair every quark lemma with an antiquark lemma; line 173 is the sole unpaired one.
findings.fix: Add `antiquark_eq_impactParameter_of_size_eq_zero {d} (h : d.size = 0) : d.antiquark = d.impactParameter`, provable by `rw [impactParameter_def, ← size_eq_zero_iff.1 h, midpoint_self]`.
findings.issue: `quark_eq_impactParameter_of_size_eq_zero` has no antiquark counterpart, although the file mirrors quark/antiquark for every other derived fact (`zero_*`, `add_*`, `neg_*`, `sub_*`, `smul_*`, `ofSizeImpactParameter_*`, `impactParameter_add_size`/`_sub_size`). The §0.1 diagonal target states both endpoints sit at `b`.

summary: The dipole/rapidity surface is mostly complete and bodies stay unexposed, but the endpoint-reconstruction lemmas the roadmap asks for as simp lemmas are unannotated, and the public unbounded `SMul S Dipole` instance exposes a scalar action with no laws and no characteristic lemmas outside `ℝ`.
